name: What is the best order to remodel an interior space?

mainEntity.name: What is the best order to remodel an interior space so I do not have to redo work later?
mainEntity.text: What is the best order to remodel an interior space so I do not have to redo work later?

acceptedAnswer.text: A well-sequenced interior remodel starts with planning, not demolition. The usual order is design, measurements, approvals, permitting, demolition, structural corrections, rough plumbing and electrical, inspections, insulation, drywall, flooring, cabinetry, countertops, fixtures, trim, paint, and final punch list. Some projects vary, but the logic stays the same: hidden systems and framing should be completed before visible finishes go in. If the order is wrong, finished materials can get damaged or have to be removed later. Homeowners should ask the contractor to explain sequencing before the job starts so they know when decisions are needed and what depends on what. Good order saves time, avoids rework, and keeps quality consistent.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best order usually starts with design and measurements, then permits, demolition, structural work, mechanical rough-ins, insulation, drywall, flooring, cabinetry, finishes, and final trim. Finishes should not be installed before hidden systems and framing are verified. Good sequencing prevents rework and protects the budget.
